name: Pastoral-Waste
specific_features: Petrified forests from a green epoch millions of years ago
Burrowing fauna adapted to extreme temperature swings
description: Pastoral-Waste is a desert world that remembers being something else. Petrified forests cover vast stretches of its badlands, stone replicas of trees that grew when the planet was green and wet, their trunks and branches preserved in mineral detail so fine that individual leaf impressions remain visible. Between the fossil forests, salt flat basins mark where lakes and inland seas once stood, their surfaces blindingly white under the thin atmosphere's unfiltered sun.

The irony of the name is intentional in survey records: this was once a pastoral world, lush and temperate, before orbital perturbations from a passing stellar neighbor shifted its axis and altered its climate over millions of years. The drying was slow enough that life adapted, retreating underground as the surface baked. Burrowing fauna now represents the dominant animal life, emerging at night to feed on the hardy surface vegetation that clings to existence in sheltered canyons and aquifer seeps.

The burrowing fauna is declining, caught in a slow extinction spiral as water tables drop and the remaining surface vegetation thins. Each generation finds fewer oases, travels farther between feeding grounds, and loses more young to the temperature extremes. Ecological projections give the current fauna perhaps fifty thousand years before the last populations collapse, an eyeblink in geological terms but an eternity by the standards of those watching it happen.

Pastoral-Waste serves as a cautionary example in terraforming ethics discussions: a world that was paradise, became wasteland through natural processes, and now presents the question of whether intervention is warranted. The technology exists to reverse the drying, but doing so would destroy the petrified forests that are the planet's most remarkable feature. The debate continues while the burrowing fauna grows scarcer, indifferent to the philosophical questions that surround its quiet, drawn-out disappearance.
